en: Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the entire Philippines, not Lake Lanao, which is only the largest lake within the Mindanao island group.
Taal Volcano is not just a single mountain, but a complex volcano featuring a main crater located on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake.
The Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the archipelago facing the Pacific Ocean, not on the western side near the South China Sea.
Palawan is officially part of the Mimaropa region in the Luzon island group, rather than being geographically classified under the Visayas island group.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect, symmetrical cone shape, unlike flat-topped mountains or irregularly shaped volcanoes like Mount Pinatubo.
Mount Pulag is the highest peak in the Luzon island group, not Mount Pinatubo, which is a prominent but shorter active stratovolcano.
The West Philippine Sea refers specifically to the eastern parts of the South China Sea within the Philippine exclusive economic zone, not the entire sea.
Mount Kanlaon is an active volcano located on Negros Island in the Visayas, not in the Mindanao island group where Mount Apo is found.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a geographic region composed of six distinct provinces, not a single unified province with one local government.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing through the Cagayan Valley, while the Pasig River is much shorter.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is a navigable waterway that flows directly into the sea, rather than just being a dead-end cave system.
The Philippines is an archipelago of over 7,600 distinct islands, not just three large continuous landmasses connected by natural land bridges.
